{{Short description|Soviet, Belarusian, and Russian mathematician}}
{{about||the Russian politician|Vladimir Platonov (politician)}}
'''Vladimir Petrovich Platonov''' ({{langx|be|Уладзімір Пятровіч Платонаў, Uladzimir Piatrovic Platonau}}; {{langx|ru|Влади́мир Петро́вич Плато́нов}}; born 1 December 1939, Stayki village, [[Vitebsk Region]], [[Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic|Byelorussian SSR]]) is a Soviet, Belarusian and Russian [[mathematician]]. He is an expert in [[algebraic geometry]] and [[topology]] and member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=ran>[http://ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-217.ln-ru.dl-.pr-inf.uk-12 Платонов Владимир Петрович] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180330012704/http://ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-217.ln-ru.dl-.pr-inf.uk-12 |date=2018-03-30 }}, profile as the [[Russian Academy of Science]] website, President of the [[Belarus Academy of Science]] (1987–1992).</ref><ref>[https://nasb.gov.by/rus/publications/vestifm/vfm00_1b.php Владимир Петрович Платонов (К 60-летию со дня рождения).] ("Vladimir Petrovich Platonov (on the occasion of the 60th anniversary)"), Известия Национальной академии наук Беларуси
СЕРИЯ ФИЗИКО-МАТЕМАТИЧЕСКИХ НАУК, No. 1, 2000, pp. 135–136</ref><ref>[http://www.ac.by/members/academicians/platonov.html Academician Vladimir P. Platonov] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041020115310/http://www.ac.by/members/academicians/platonov.html |date=2004-10-20 }}, Belarusian Academy of Sciences</ref>

From 1992–2004 he worked at research centers in the [[United States]], [[Canada]] and [[Germany]].<ref name=ran/>

== Education ==

In 1961 Platonov graduated with highest distinction from [[Belarusian State University]]. In 1963 he received his Ph.D. from the Academy of Sciences of Belarus. In 1967, Platonov received his Doctor of Science degree from the Academy of Sciences of USSR.

== Career ==
At age 28 Platonov received a title of full professor at Belarus State. This made him the youngest full professor in the nation's history. In 1972 he became an Academician of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]] and its President (1987–1993).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ac.by/members/academicians/platonov.html|title=Academician Vladimir P. Platonov|publisher=Belarusian Academy of Sciences|access-date=2004-08-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041020115310/http://www.ac.by/members/academicians/platonov.html|archive-date=2004-10-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has been an Academician of the Russian/USSR Academy of Sciences since 1987. He was the Director of the Institute of Mathematics of the Academy of Sciences of Belarus from 1977 to 1992.

== Research ==
His interests are [[algebra]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[number theory]]. He solved the Strong approximation problem, developed the reduced [[Algebraic K-theory|K-theory]] and solved the [[Tannaka–Artin problem]].<ref>V. P. Platonov, "The Tanaka–Artin problem and reduced K-theory," Izv. [[USSR Academy of Sciences|Akad. Nauk SSSR]],. Ser. Mat., 40:2, 1976, pp. 227–261 ({{in lang|ru}} [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/person.phtml?option_lang=rus&personid=9012 Проблема Таннака–Артина и приведенная ''K''-теория])</ref> He solved the [[Kneser–Tits conjecture|Kneser-Tits]] and Grothendieck problems. Together with F. Grunewald he solved the arithmeticity problem for finite extensions of arithmetic groups and the rigidity problem for arithmetic subgroups of algebraic groups with radical. Platonov solved the rationality problem for [[spinor]] varieties and the Dieudonne problem on [[Orthogonal group|spinor norms]].

Platonov was an invited speaker of the International Congresses of Mathematicians in Vancouver (1974), Helsinki (1978) and the European Congress of Mathematicians in Budapest (1996).

He is a member of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] and from 1993 to 2001 was a Professor of the [[University of Waterloo Faculty of Mathematics|Faculty of Mathematics]] of the [[University of Waterloo]] in [[Waterloo, Ontario]], [[Canada]].

He is the author, with Andrei Rapinchuk, of ''Algebraic Groups and Number Theory''.<ref>Vladimir Platonov, Andrei Rapinchuk, ''Algebraic Groups and Number Theory'', Academic Press, 1993, {{ISBN|978-0-12-558180-6}}, {{in lang|ru}} [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/journal.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=rm&paperid=4493&year=1992&volume=47&issue=2&fpage=117&lpage=141&option_lang=rus Алгебраические группы и теория чисел], [[Uspekhi mathematicheskikh nauk|УМН]], 1992, No. 47:2 (284), pp. 117–141</ref>

He currently works as a Chief Science Officer of [[Scientific Research Institute of System Development]] (NIISI RAN).<ref>{{in lang|ru}} [http://www.niisi.ru/platonov.htm Vladimir Platonov] at [[NIISI]] website</ref>

== Assault conviction ==
On November 9, 1999, Platonov appeared in court on a bail hearing on a charge of [[attempted murder]] for an attack on his wife.<ref>{{cite news|title=Prof charged with attempted murder|url=https://www.bulletin.uwaterloo.ca/1999/nov/09tu.html|newspaper=Waterloo Daily Bulletin |date=Nov 9, 1999}}</ref> He was convicted of assault.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://newsrelease.uwaterloo.ca/news.php?id=2320|title=Statement on Prof. Vladimir Platonov|date=19 January 2018 |publisher=University of Waterloo Communications & Public Affairs}}</ref> The court gave him a conditional sentence of two years. In September 2001, Platonov took early retirement as a professor of the University of Waterloo.

==Awards==
*[[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]]
*1968: [[Lenin Komsomol Prize]], for a series of works in [[topological group]] theory
*1978: [[Lenin Prize]] in Science and Technology, for a fundamental series of works "Arithmetics of Algebraic Groups and Reduced [[K-theory|K-Theory]]" ("Арифметика алгебраических групп и приведенная К-теория")
*1993: [[Humboldt Prize]]
